title: DUSRM 0.2 Pilot — SAND OS Operating-System Architecture
summary: Repository-informed SAND OS architecture description. Current prototype capabilities are separated from planned userland and production capabilities.

systemOfInterest.name: SAND OS
systemOfInterest.description: Independent OS research project with a SAND-authored legacy-BIOS x86 boot chain, 32-bit kernel, early process/storage subsystems, Veyra interface foundation and SAPP application format.

context.purpose: Describe SAND OS responsibilities, boundaries, interfaces, persistent formats, maturity and evidence without adding runtime dependencies.
context.scope: Current SAND-authored boot, kernel, memory, scheduling, process, syscall, storage, SANDFS, Veyra, graphics/windowing and SAPP components; future services are marked planned.

boundary.notes: DUSRM is a design-time architecture description and validation method, not part of the kernel image or runtime.

environment.name: Legacy BIOS x86 target platform
environment.description: Current boot path targets legacy BIOS and 32-bit x86 protected mode.

environment.name: QEMU System i386
environment.description: External emulator for development and automated boot tests; not part of the SAND runtime.

environment.name: Host build toolchain
environment.description: GCC, GNU Binutils, Make and Python are host-side tools.

environment.name: SAPP application image
environment.description: Versioned SAPP container supplied to the process loader; signatures and trust-store are not implemented.

assumptions: Repository documentation and CI are project evidence, not independent hardware or security certification.
The current target is legacy-BIOS x86-32; UEFI and x86-64 support are not established.
SAND's nine implementation strata do not map one-to-one to DUSRM's eight responsibility layers.
DUSRM validation remains external to SAND boot and runtime.
README milestone text conflicts with detailed architecture and roadmap text; milestone numbering is not used as the sole maturity authority.

elements.name: SAND boot chain
elements.description: SAND-authored boot sector and second-stage loader for bounded raw kernel payload loading and 32-bit protected-mode handoff.

elements.name: x86 architecture support
elements.description: Architecture-specific x86-32 support and early platform drivers.

elements.name: SAND kernel core
elements.description: Freestanding 32-bit kernel hosting SAND-owned subsystem policies and self-tests.

elements.name: Memory manager
elements.description: Early bounded physical-frame allocator, non-PAE paging and page-backed bump heap; production VM features remain incomplete.

elements.name: Kernel scheduler and synchronization
elements.description: Uniprocessor kernel-thread scheduler and basic synchronization prototype; not SMP-safe or production hardened.

elements.name: Process manager
elements.description: Bounded process table and distinct user address spaces; no complete preemptive user-process scheduler or robust fault isolation.

elements.name: System-call gateway
elements.description: Limited syscall proof-of-concept; a general-purpose safe syscall ABI and complete user-pointer validation are not established.

elements.name: Block-device abstraction
elements.description: SAND-owned block-device registration interface with sector callbacks.

elements.name: Primary-master ATA PIO driver
elements.description: Initial polling-only primary-master ATA PIO backend, not a general storage driver framework.

elements.name: SANDFS v1
elements.description: Versioned one-sector-per-file filesystem prototype; lacks journaling, crash consistency, checksums, permissions and concurrent-access locks.

elements.name: SAND Veyra interface foundation
elements.description: Versioned descriptor/status foundation; not a complete general-purpose syscall ABI or IPC facility.

elements.name: Framebuffer and windowing prototype
elements.description: Early framebuffer/windowing functionality; no complete compositor, application surfaces or desktop event loop.

elements.name: SAPP v0.2 format and SDK
elements.description: Custom SAPP container and builder; signing, trust store, filesystem launch, shared libraries and dynamic linker remain incomplete.

elements.name: Network stack and services
elements.description: Future roadmap work; no working SAND network stack is claimed.

elements.name: Service IPC and supervision
elements.description: IPC and service contracts are future Veyra gaps; not implemented.

elements.name: Native desktop compositor
elements.description: Planned native desktop subsystem; the current framebuffer/window prototypes are not a complete compositor.

responsibilities.name: Establish platform entry and execution context
responsibilities.description: Interact with target firmware/CPU platform and establish controlled transition into the SAND kernel.

responsibilities.name: Manage memory, execution and device resources
responsibilities.description: Allocate and constrain physical frames, kernel memory, process slots, thread slots and block-device access within current prototype limits.

responsibilities.name: Control boot, interrupt, thread and process execution
responsibilities.description: Sequence boot operations, handle interrupts, schedule kernel threads and manage bounded process lifecycle operations.

responsibilities.name: Maintain kernel, process and persistent filesystem state
responsibilities.description: Represent execution states, address-space state, filesystem metadata and versioned application-container contents.

responsibilities.name: Compute address translation, scheduling and image validation
responsibilities.description: Perform paging decisions, runnable-thread selection, format validation and kernel/userland transformations.

responsibilities.name: Expose controlled kernel and subsystem interfaces
responsibilities.description: Provide versioned SAND-owned descriptors, syscall entry and future ABI/service boundaries while preserving privilege separation.

responsibilities.name: Provide native storage, graphics and application services
responsibilities.description: Offer file, block-device, windowing and application-package capabilities with explicit prototype limitations.

responsibilities.name: Provide an independent general-purpose operating system
responsibilities.description: Deliver a complete, secure and usable OS with stable userland, drivers, storage, networking, graphical desktop, native apps and release engineering.

realizations.rationale: SAND-authored BIOS boot stages establish the current platform entry path; support is limited to legacy BIOS x86-32.
The memory manager implements early frame allocation, paging and heap management.
The kernel hosts boot, interrupt, scheduling and process-management prototypes.
Process descriptors and page-directory mappings represent process lifecycle and address-space state.
The scheduler selects runnable execution contexts under the current prototype policy.
Veyra supplies the shared descriptor/status foundation; general ABI and IPC remain incomplete.
SANDFS implements a small native storage prototype; graphics and SAPP provide additional early facilities.

layerApplicability.rationale: The target relies on external legacy BIOS and x86 hardware/firmware; SAND provides its own boot and architecture code.
Memory, thread, process and storage resource management are internal kernel responsibilities.
Boot sequencing, interrupts, scheduling and process lifecycle are within the system boundary.
Process/thread state, filesystem metadata and executable package state are represented.
Paging, scheduler selection and application-image validation provide computation/transformation responsibilities.
Syscall and Veyra descriptor contracts define interaction boundaries; a stable general-purpose ABI remains incomplete.
Storage, graphics/windowing and SAPP developer facilities are in scope as prototypes.
The general-purpose OS outcome is in scope but is not yet realized as a complete product.

relationships.rationale: The boot chain is an internal constituent of SAND OS.
The kernel delegates memory-management responsibilities to a dedicated subsystem.
The current boot path depends on legacy BIOS and x86 platform services.
Veyra is the published interface architecture for SAND-owned ABI and subsystem contracts.
Process and user-mode integration depends on safe SAND-owned interface contracts.
The SAPP toolchain and kernel SAPP loading path interact across the executable-container boundary.
The bounded process manager owns a fixed number of process descriptors.
SANDFS is an internal SAND-owned filesystem prototype.
The illustrative execution record references the bounded process creation operation; it is not an additional runtime test.
A process creation request triggers the modeled transition into the ready state after successful setup.
The process lifecycle includes a created-to-ready transition.
The SDK and packer implement the SAPP container specification within current development limits.

operations.name: BootKernel
operations.purpose: Load the bounded kernel payload, establish the initial CPU mode and transfer control to the kernel entry point.
preconditions: Target firmware provides the assumed legacy BIOS services
Kernel payload fits documented loader bounds
postconditions: Control reaches the kernel entry point in 32-bit protected mode

operations.name: CreateProcessAddressSpace
operations.purpose: Create a bounded process record and distinct user address-space resources.
preconditions: User mappings fall within the reserved user range
postconditions: A process descriptor and page directory are created

operations.name: MountSANDFS
operations.purpose: Validate the SANDFS superblock and bounded metadata before exposing the filesystem prototype.
preconditions: The selected LBA range is within device bounds
postconditions: SANDFS is mounted for documented limited operations

executions.context: Illustrative architecture execution; not evidence of an additional runtime test.

states.meaning: Process resources are being initialized or have been allocated but are not yet ready.
The process is eligible for later scheduling when a complete user-process scheduler exists.
SANDFS metadata was accepted and the limited filesystem API is available.

transitions.guard: Process record and required user address-space resources are initialized successfully.
Superblock, format version, LBA bounds and directory metadata validation succeed.
transitions.effect: Expose the bounded SANDFS read/write operations.

interfaces.name: SAND Veyra interface descriptor foundation
interfaces.description: Versioned descriptor/status foundation. It does not assert that general IPC or a stable general-purpose syscall ABI exists.

interactions.name: Kernel subsystem consumes a Veyra contract

resources.name: Process descriptor slots
resources.description: Compile-time bounded process table limit in the current process header; not a scalable capacity guarantee.

allocations.policy: Bounded static process descriptor table; future dynamic allocation is not implied.

capabilities.name: Bounded process address-space lifecycle
capabilities.description: Create, activate, terminate and destroy process address spaces within current prototype limits.

capabilities.name: SANDFS v1 limited file storage
capabilities.description: Format, mount and read/write files within the fixed-directory, one-sector-per-file prototype.
preconditions: A compatible block device is registered
limitations: No permissions or concurrent access locks
Small fixed directory and file-size limits

services.name: Process management service boundary
services.description: Kernel-owned process management operations used by boot tests and future SAPP launch facilities.
qualityConstraints: No stable general-purpose application ABI is implied

requirements.statement: Architecture-specific code shall remain behind interfaces consumed by the kernel core.
acceptanceCriteria: Architecture-specific code has explicit SAND-owned subsystem boundaries

requirements.statement: User applications shall not execute in kernel privilege level.
acceptanceCriteria: User application execution uses user privilege mappings
Kernel structures are not exposed as unrestricted user authority

requirements.statement: Persistent storage formats and executable containers shall be versioned and validated.
acceptanceCriteria: SAPP format version and segment bounds are validated

constraints.statement: The resulting SAND OS runtime shall not depend on a Linux kernel or another pre-existing general-purpose OS runtime.
QEMU and the host compiler/build toolchain remain external development/test tools and are not included in the OS runtime.
SAND OS is experimental research software and must not be described as production-secure or suitable for sensitive workloads.
Unsigned SAPP packages are development artifacts; production signing and trust-store verification are not implemented.

invariants.statement: A SAPP v1 load segment must not be simultaneously writable and executable.
assumptions: The invariant is stated by the format specification; the complete runtime enforcement path requires separate review.
invariants.method: Specification/CI mapping; not an independent security assessment.

invariants.statement: Kernel-private mappings and interfaces must not be exposed as unrestricted user-mode authority.
assumptions: Current process and syscall path is a prototype; safe user-pointer validation is incomplete.
invariants.method: Architecture review requirement; not a verified security property.

assertions.statement: The latest inspected SAND OS Native Boot CI run passed boot-image build, SDK/ABI host checks and QEMU self-tests at the inspected repository head.
The repository explicitly describes SAND OS as experimental research software and not suitable for production or safety-critical use.

decisions.title: DUSRM remains a design-time architecture and validation dependency only
decisions.statement: DUSRM descriptions and validation may govern SAND subsystem boundaries, but DUSRM is not linked into the boot chain, kernel image, runtime or SAPP container.
decisions.rationale: Preserves SAND runtime independence and avoids introducing a second kernel API or boot dependency.

decisions.title: Map SAND architecture strata to DUSRM layers many-to-many
decisions.statement: SAND's nine implementation strata are mapped to DUSRM's eight responsibility layers by responsibility; neither model mirrors the other's number or ordering.
decisions.rationale: DUSRM layers are responsibility categories, while SAND strata are implementation organization and dependency boundaries.

evidence.description: SAND OS README establishes the independent OS objective and current legacy-BIOS x86-32 boot path, but labels current status M0 while detailed architecture, roadmap and CI describe later subsystems.
limitations: README milestone text conflicts with detailed architecture and roadmap; do not use its M0 label as sole maturity evidence.

evidence.description: SAND OS architecture document describes boot, x86 architecture, memory, scheduler, process, filesystem and graphics prototypes with limitations.
limitations: Documentation is not independent physical-hardware or security verification.

evidence.description: SAND OS roadmap records M0–M13 and intended exit evidence.
limitations: Roadmap entries are plans and do not by themselves establish implementation.

evidence.description: Veyra catalogue distinguishes implemented, prototype and future interfaces and lists missing IPC, service and stable ABI facilities.
limitations: Presence of a header does not establish a stable public interface.

evidence.description: Veyra foundation defines versioned descriptors and status conventions while explicitly stating the general-purpose syscall ABI is incomplete.
limitations: Descriptor helper is for trusted readable memory and does not make arbitrary user pointers safe.

evidence.description: SAPP format specifies header, segments, relocations, W+X rejection and development-only unsigned packages.
limitations: Signing, trust-store verification and complete production launch path are not implemented.

evidence.description: SAPP SDK README states v0.2 packer, multi-segment packaging, BSS, permissions, relocations and process_create_sapp integration.
limitations: Filesystem launch, shared libraries, dynamic linker and production signing/trust are absent.

evidence.description: Architecture document describes SANDFS as a versioned one-sector-per-file prototype with explicit restrictions.
limitations: No journal, crash consistency, checksums, permissions or concurrent access locks; not for important data.

evidence.description: SAND process header defines a compile-time bounded process table and lifecycle API.
limitations: Header presence does not establish a complete general-purpose process scheduler.

evidence.description: Scheduler header defines SAND_SCHEDULER_MAX_THREADS as 8 while architecture narrative describes four thread descriptors/stacks; record as source consistency question.
limitations: A header constant alone does not prove the active scheduler table/stack count; reconcile with implementation and tests.

evidence.description: Security policy explicitly states experimental status and absence of production-grade security boundary, verified boot, sandbox, cryptographic update or security audit.
limitations: Project policy/status, not an independent security audit.

evidence.description: Build instructions define Linux/WSL host toolchain and QEMU test environment, not runtime dependencies.
limitations: Build instructions are not evidence of physical hardware support.

evidence.description: SAND OS Native Boot CI run #42876341368 passed on the inspected main commit 661cdedd38e2e24e202dee22798047fd7311353a. It ran make clean/check, SAPP unit tests, Veyra descriptor host tests and booted the image in QEMU with kernel self-test assertions.
evidence.resultSummary: Workflow conclusion success; host checks and QEMU kernel self-test assertions completed.
limitations: QEMU results do not prove physical hardware compatibility, production security, broad filesystem correctness or stable general-purpose user ABI.

org.dmj.dusrm.profile.operating-system.mappingRule: SAND implementation strata and DUSRM responsibility layers are different classification systems. Mapping is many-to-many, descriptive and does not imply an execution order.
org.dmj.dusrm.profile.operating-system.adoptionMode: design-time architecture description plus CI validation; no kernel/runtime dependency

implementationStrata.name: Architecture-specific CPU, interrupt, paging and context-switch code
Kernel core: memory, scheduler, synchronization, IPC and object model

prohibitedClaims: QEMU tests are not physical hardware verification.
Veyra descriptor headers are not a complete syscall/IPC ABI.
SANDFS v1 is not a production filesystem.
